newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat ends lower, led by Dec on deliveries.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat ends lower, led by Dec on deliveries.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures closed lower, led by December, on the posting of just over one million bushels of wheat for delivery on that contract, traders said.
"The deliveries on December led it down," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter Reynolds.
There were 1.150 million bushels of wheat posted Wednesday for delivery on the December amid weak stoppers. CBOT data showed Refco Inc put out 550,000 bushels.
The balance of the delivery tally was redelivery of the wheat notices posted Tuesday, traders said.
Export news provided little direction, with keen competition from other key world wheat producers limiting gains.

Reports circulated that a Bangladesh tender for 100,000 tonnes of optional-origin wheat was delayed, South Korea passed on a tender for 105,000 tonnes of feed wheat and Taiwan bought 72,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat for Dec/Jan delivery.
Some traders said a drop in the Dow Jones Industrial stock index may have lent further pressure to wheat futures.
Wheat closed 1/2 to 6-3/4 cents per bushel lower, with December down 6-3/4 at $3.78-1/4. March was down 1-3/4 at $3.70-1/4 a bushel.
The market early attempted to stage a recovery but faltered in late dealings. The early strength in wheat was tied to a technical bounce.
"A little short covering. Five days in a row down so it's giving a little back," said Skip Searcy, wheat trading specialist for FIMAT Futures.
Key players included Refco Inc selling 1.0 million bushels of March and bought 1.5 million March, traders said. Also, Cargill Investor Services sold one million bushels of March, sources said.
Wheat futures volume was estimated at 16,000 contracts, below the 16,102 traded Tuesday, according to the CBOT.
In wheat options, LFG Futures bought 400 May $3.40 puts and sold 400 July $3.00 puts at 6-1/2 cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated by the CBOT at 3,000 contracts, below the 4,514 traded Tuesday.
